chunks: Whoever proceeds towards this mischief will be ruined, and whoever strives for it will be annihilated.
They will be biting each other during it as the wild asses bite each other in the herd.
The coils of the rope will be disturbed and the face of affairs will be blinded.
During it sagacity will be on the ebb, and the oppressors will (get the opportunity to) speak.
This mischief will smash the Bedouins with its hammers and crush them with its chest.
In its dust the single marchers will be lost, and in its way the horsemen will be destroyed.
It will approach with the bitterness of destiny and will give pure blood (instead of milk).
It will breach the minarets of faith and shatter the ties of firm belief.
The wise will run away from it while the wicked will foster it.
It will thunder and flash (like lightning). It will create a severe disaster.
In it kinship will be forsaken and Islam will be abandoned.
He who declaims it will also be affected by it, and he who flees from it will (be forced to) stay in it.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the period of great disorder (fitnah) described in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Scholars interpret this vivid imagery as a description of the 'Great Calamity' (al-Fatwa al-Kubra) or the era of Umayyad oppression, where political authority was seized by the unworthy ('al-irjas') while wisdom was marginalized. The metaphor of the 'garment being lifted' alludes to the exposure of hidden truths and the breakdown of social order, serving as a warning to the faithful to maintain spiritual integrity amidst widespread injustice.
